statements.text: All three readings can be normal for healthy people because 37.0 °C is a typical average, not an exact value every person must show.
Anyone not exactly 37.0 °C after play is unhealthy.
A reading of 41.5 °C can also be normal for a healthy sibling.

stem: Ishaan records evening body temperatures of three healthy siblings after play: 36.7 °C, 37.1 °C, and 37.3 °C. A chart marks about 37.0 °C as a typical average and shows 41.5 °C as a very high fever reading.

teacher.key_rationale: 37.0 °C is a useful average; small differences around it can still be healthy. Exact 37.0 °C is not required, and 41.5 °C is not a normal healthy reading.
